title: THA Product Knowledge Registry — Inventory Schema v1
description: Validates the machine-readable inventory generated from docs/product/inventory/product.yaml. Governed by docs/architecture/THA_PRODUCT_KNOWLEDGE_REGISTRY_ARCHITECTURE.md §10.2. The `visibility` field is mandatory and fails closed (Rule PKR22): an entry with a missing or unrecognised visibility is treated as `developer` and served to no one — it never defaults to `public`.

entry.description: The entry spine fixed by PKR §7. Sections may add fields; none may remove these.

id.description: Stable, unique, permanent. Never reused, never renumbered, never reissued after retirement (PKR §7, §17).

section.description: One of the 28 canonical sections fixed by PKR §8. Exactly one.

visibility.description: The LOWEST audience permitted to be told this. Monotonic: developer ⊇ admin ⊇ household ⊇ public (Rule PKR23). Mandatory; fails closed to `developer` (Rule PKR22).

purpose.description: What it is for, in one sentence, in the household's terms — not the engineer's (PKR §7).

owner.description: A named human. Not a team, not a workstream, not 'the platform' (Rule PKR12).

sources.description: Pointers to code, route, table, Capability Card or SoT Register domain. Pointers only — never restatements (Rule PKR1).

related.description: Other registry ids. The graph of the product.

last_verified.description: The date a human last confirmed this is still true. Older than 90 days is PRESUMED STALE (PKR §15.3).

known_defects.description: Citations into the investigation that discovered the defect (PDA1). NOT registry ids — `related` is the graph of the product and holds registry ids only. An entry records that a surface exists and what it is for; the defect is history, and history lives in the investigation.

substantiated_by.description: Registry ids of the product truth substantiating a claim. A Marketing Message, Benefit or Competitive Advantage with an empty list and no stated substantiation_gap is a fabrication and must not enter the registry (PKR §8 s20).

substantiation_gap.description: Stated honestly where a claim outruns the product. Its presence is what keeps an unsubstantiated claim admissible as a KNOWN gap rather than a lie.
